markdown_content: ## Introduction to Using MetaHumans in Clo3D and Unreal Engine This section explains the initial setup for integrating MetaHumans with Clo3D and Unreal Engine, covering plugin activation, MetaHuman creation, and preparing assets for garment design. Key terms include MetaHuman Creator Core Data, Clo3D, Unreal Engine 5.6, and Epic Games Launcher. To begin, open the Epic Games Launcher Library, click the arrow next to Launch, and enable **MetaHuman Creator Core Data** for your project. Launch Unreal Engine and go to **Edit > Plugins**. Enable the **Clo3D plugin** and **MetaHuman Creator Core Data** plugin, then restart Unreal Engine to apply changes. Next, open the Content Browser in Unreal Engine. Right-click, select **MetaHuman > MetaHuman Character** to create a new MetaHuman character. Double-click the new MetaHuman asset to open the MetaHuman Editor in Unreal Engine 5.6, where you can customize your character. ## Importing MetaHuman Body into Clo3D and Adding Garments This section details how to import MetaHuman body data into Clo3D, add garments, and prepare UV maps for exporting. It includes file formats, import procedures, and export settings necessary for Unreal Engine integration. Export the MetaHuman DNA file for Clo3D by selecting your output folder and clicking the appropriate export option. In Clo3D, go to **File > Import DNA**, and select your exported DNA file. First, import the body file, then the head file. This imports your MetaHuman body into Clo3D. Add garments such as a skirt and a turtleneck to the character and fit them properly. Use Clo3D’s **UV Editor** and apply the **Auto UV Packing** tool to generate UV maps for the garments. Export the garment as a **USD (Universal Scene Description)** file. In the export settings, ensure you select: - Include Garment - Select All Patterns - Single Object - Unified UV Coordinates - Export all required texture maps - Include garment simulation data Return to Unreal Engine after exporting. ## Setting Up a Resizable MetaHuman Outfit Asset in Unreal Engine This section covers organizing assets, importing garment files, creating cloth assets, and setting up a resizable outfit using Unreal Engine’s Content Browser and Data Flow Graph. It explains folder structure, USD import, skeletal mesh export, and cloth asset creation. In Unreal Engine’s Content Browser, organize your project by creating an **Outfits** folder. Inside it, create a subfolder named after your asset (e.g., "Style1"). Import the USD garment file into this folder. The import process will create a "Style1" folder containing three subfolders; focus mainly on **Static Meshes** for cloth asset creation. Go to the **Meshes** folder, select your MetaHuman, and export the **combined skeletal mesh**. Save it in the MetaHuman folder. Close the MetaHuman Editor. In the Static Meshes folder, right-click and create a **Physics Cloth Asset**, naming it distinctively. This action creates a Data Flow (DF) node, which is essential and should remain unchanged. Open the DF node by right-clicking and selecting **Open > Data Flow Editor (Experimental)**. Clear unnecessary nodes, retaining only **Transfer Skin Weights**, **Remesh nodes**, and **Cloth Asset Terminal nodes**. Delete purple and brown nodes to simplify the graph. Right-click to add: - A **Static Mesh Import** node and select the Static Mesh of your outfit (Style1). - Ensure **Import Simulation Mesh** is unchecked if you do not have simulation mesh data. Configure the **Transfer Skin Weights** node: - Select Render Mesh and Skeletal Mesh. - Choose your combined MetaHuman skeletal mesh. - Set Transfer Method to **Closest Point on Surface**. Connect nodes as follows: - Static Mesh Import to Transfer Skin Weights collection. - Transfer Skin Weights collection to Cloth Asset Terminal node. - Transfer Skin Weights collection to Remesh collection. - Remesh collection to Collection LOD 1. In the construction viewport, verify the asset appears correctly, currently set to LOD 1. You can toggle the render view in the top-right. Save your project. ## Finalizing and Applying the Outfit Asset to MetaHumans This section explains creating the outfit asset, configuring the Data Flow Graph evaluator, and applying the outfit to a new MetaHuman character in Unreal Engine. In the Content Browser’s main folder (containing only your working folder), right-click and select **Physics > Outfit Asset**. Name this asset (e.g., Style1) and select **Resizable Outfit**. Move the Data Flow node into the working folder so only the outfit asset remains in the main folder. Open the outfit asset and in the top-right corner, click the three dots beside **Evaluate Data Flow Graph**. Select **Manual Graph Evaluator** to avoid long evaluation times. In the **Data Flow Members** panel (bottom left), check **Sized Outfit Source** and add an entry for each cloth asset. For each, select the Source Asset (your CA Style1 cloth asset) and Source Body Parts (Character 1 Combined Skeletal Mesh). If you have multiple sizes, add additional entries. Click **Evaluate Data Flow Graph**, then switch back to **Automatic Evaluation** once complete. Save and close the outfit asset window. To test the outfit, create a new MetaHuman in the Content Browser (e.g., "Character 2"). Open its MetaHuman Editor, go to the **Hair & Clothing** tab, scroll to the **Cloth** section, and remove any current outfit. Drag and drop your outfit asset from the Content Browser into the current outfit slot. The outfit will appear on the new MetaHuman. You can now adjust the outfit size dynamically, and the clothing will respond accordingly. ## Summary This guide covers: - Enabling necessary plugins for MetaHuman and Clo3D integration - Importing MetaHuman body data into Clo3D and adding garments - Exporting garments as USD files with simulation data - Organizing and importing assets in Unreal Engine - Creating cloth assets using Data Flow Graph Editor - Setting up resizable outfit assets linked to MetaHumans - Applying and testing outfits on new MetaHuman characters with dynamic resizing These steps enable designers to create customizable digital garments for MetaHumans using Clo3D and Unreal Engine, facilitating advanced character wardrobe workflows for game development and virtual production.
